newsitem.title: HUNGARY: E.EURO.FOOD FUND ACQUIRES STAKE IN CSOPAK.
newsitem.headline: E.EURO.FOOD FUND ACQUIRES STAKE IN CSOPAK.

text.p: U.K-based East European Food Fund acquired a just over 30 percent stake in Hungarian holding firm Csopak Rt after Csopak's shareholders approved the transaction on Monday, Csopak officials told a news conference.

Making its third investment in Hungary, the fund subscribed the whole of a 700-million-forint private share issue which brought Csopak's issued share capital to 2.2 billion. The 1,000-forint face value shares were issued at 1,150 forints.

"What encouraged us about Csopak was that it had already been progressive in expanding and consolidating its activities, had a good profit and growth record and...has firm plans to expand," said Laurie Cannon, Director of Jupiter Asset Management, which launched the fund.
Cannon declined to say what Jupiter's other two investments were.
Csopak's General Director Gyorgy Markovszky said the appearance of the foreign shareholder will allow Csopak to confirm its strategy of enhancing trading within the group.
"Csopak will quit the role of holding company and wishes to be a trading house," he said, adding in a statement that the company will focus on the development of food trading.
Markovszky Csopak intends to operate more shopping centres in western Hungary in addition to the two it runs now, he said.
The company, located in Nemesvamos, in western Hungary, is currently also involved in milling and cosmetics industries.
With the fund's appearance Hungarian bank MBFB reduced its stake to around 30 percent from above 50 percent and said it wishes to cut it further.

"In the long-term...we wish to reduce our stake," MBFB's General Director Andras Huszty, who was elected to Csopak's board today, said. Such a move will come once the company reaches a level of development which will allow the bank to lock in acceptable profits from share price increases.
Markovszky said the Csopak group expects to post around 500 million forints of after-tax profit on sales of seven billion in 1996.
On Monday Csopak shares closed at 1,165 forints, up 25.
